Subject Reported Japanese plan to monopolize the egg trade in China.

Made by D.S. Kamashita Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

With reference to the attached extract from the
China Press dated January 8, 1940, regarding the report
that a large Japanese firm had been established to mono-
polize the egg trade in China, I have to state that
enquiries were made at the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and that
the report contained in the article is incorrect.
Although the egg trade occupies an important part
of China's exports, no Japanese firm or individual en-
gaged in this trade before the Sino-Japanese hostilities.
Following the removal of the fighting zone from Shanghai,
the Japanese military authorities suggested that Japanese
firms take up this business, as a result of which the
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha commenced the egg business in the
premises of the Shanghai Storage & Trust Company, a
Japanese firm at No. 1080 East Broadway, about one year
ago and later the factory of the China Egg Produce Co.,
a Chinese concern, 50 Minghong Road, was reorganized into
a Sino-Japanese company, known as the Yangtsze Egg &
Cold Storage Co. which is at present placed under the
management of the M.B.K. After the Japanese occupation
of lower Yangtsze district and owing to the existence
of control on transportation, according to an official
of the M.B.K., eggs purchased in the interior districts
by foreign merchants were brought here in Japanese mili-
tary transports on behalf of purchasers.

CHINA PRESS.
JAN 8 1940
Japanese Firm Is Organized To
Effect China Egg Monopoly

A large Japanese combine, believed to be a subsidiary of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, has been established to complete the Japanese plan of monopolizing China's enormous egg trade, thus driving out all legitimate foreign interests, Chinese quarters revealed last night.

Known as Cheng Hwa Company in Chinese, the new commercial enterprise, according to reports, came into existence on New Year's Day. Its agencies were said to be located at all egg producing districts in the occupied areas.

Sending its buyers deep into small villages, this six-day old organization functioning with the aid of the Japanese military and local puppet regimes has already cut severely into the dwindling trading opportunities of both Chinese and foreign establishments.

It was pointed out that if the activities of this new enterprise be kept up at their present pace, before long all the egg trade which in ordinary times amounted to tens of millions of dollars each year would dwindle to nothing for all Chinese and foreign firms except for the Japanese concern.

Japanese plans to hold a monopoly over the China egg trade were revealed in mid-October when a large foreign firm informed the local press that huge quantities of its shipments, as well as those of other firms, had been appropriated by Japanese agents employed by the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.

At the time, the Japanese internationally-known firm, in replying to inquiries, stated that it was acting under instructions from Japanese military authorities. They later promised to release the seized shipments after repeated protests addressed to the Japanese through their consular authorities. The promise, however, had never been carried out although small quantities of eggs were permitted to be brought to Shanghai by buyers of the foreign firms.

It could not be ascertained last night what action foreign egg merchants here would take to combat this new Japanese move to complete their monopolistic designs.

1940年1月8日
日本商社组建以实现中国蛋业垄断

据中方人士昨晚透露，一家大型日本联合体（被认为是三井物产株式会社的子公司）已经成立，旨在完成日本垄断中国庞大蛋业贸易的计划，从而将所有合法的外国利益驱逐出去。

据报道，这家新的商业企业中文名为“成华公司”（Cheng Hwa Company），于元旦当天成立。据说其在所有被占领区的产蛋地区都设有代理机构。

这家成立仅六天的组织在日本军队和当地傀儡政权的协助下运作，派遣买家深入小村庄，已经严重削减了华商和外商日益减少的交易机会。

有人指出，如果这家新企业的活动保持目前的步伐，不久之后，除了日本商社外，所有中外商社每年通常价值数千万美元的蛋业贸易都将萎缩至无。

日本计划垄断中国蛋业贸易的消息在十月中旬曝光，当时一家大型外国商社告知当地媒体，其大量货物以及其他商社的货物已被三井物产株式会社雇用的日本代理人侵占。

当时，这家国际知名的日本商社在回复询问时表示，它是按照日本军方当局的指示行事。后来，在通过领事当局向日本方面多次抗议后，他们承诺释放被扣押的货物。然而，这一承诺从未兑现，尽管允许外国商社的买家将少量鸡蛋运入上海。

昨晚尚无法确定在沪的外国蛋商将采取何种行动来对抗日本完成其垄断图谋的这一新举动。

Sir,
The victim of this alleged abduction presented himself at Central Station on the evening of November 10 after being presumably held in captivity for one week by his abductors.
In addition to being abducted he alleges that he was relieved of the sum of $1,164.00 and during captivity was asked to write letters with a view to inducing payment of more money.
He gave a vague and hazy account of what actually took place and this coupled with his utter inability to give the slightest information regarding his abductors' rendezvous is looked upon with suspicion.
There is something very strange about the whole affair and the failure of the only eye-witness (Oen Tsung Tai) to come forward to substantiate the victim's statement gives credence to the opinion held by detectives that his disappearance was for some purpose which he is not prepared to disclose.

我是泰州“陆公记”蛋行的合伙人，我在该行投资了1,000美元作为我的股份。
1939年10月30日上午6点，在新港（Sing Kong，音译）和泰州购买了32篮鸡蛋后，我通过“鹤形丸”号轮船（s/s "Tsurugata Maru"）运送这些鸡蛋，该船于1939年11月1日下午2点抵达日清码头（N.Y.K.Wayside Wharf）。随后我乘渡轮上岸（13号浮码头），前往法租界马思南路14号的利达蛋行（Lih Dah Egg Co.），在那里收取了一笔金额为$k,529.00（原文不清，疑似$4,529.00或类似数字）的蛋款。我又从汉口路与浙江路路口的中源泰蛋行（Zung Yuen Tah Egg Co.，音译）收取了2,104.00美元。

Reported Abduction of a Chinese Egg Merchant

Sir,
A report to the effect that one named Chang Sheu
Shan (張寿山) had been abducted by five armed men at
No.4 Pontoon, The Bund, was made at the Bund Sub-
Station by one named Pan Yoong Chiang (潘永章) at
8.30p.m. November 3, 1939.

Investigations revealed that the victim of the
alleged abduction is an egg merchant and a native of
Taichow to which place he was about to proceed when
the incident took place. He is reported to reside
in Pootung.

The affair is shrouded in mystery and there is
at present no evidence whatsoever to substantiate

CHINA PRESS.
Japanese Said Reducing Egg
Packers Here To Jobbers

By PAUL FENG
Press reports circulated yesterday stating that the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha had abandoned its monopolistic plan in the enormous egg business in China could not be confirmed in well-informed circles here.
An egg dealer told THE CHINA PRESS that "it is far from the truth that the Japanese have any intention of allowing free passage of eggs through the Yangtse delta to Shanghai."
He pointed out that this was not to say that foreign packers here could no longer obtain supplies. "If they want," he said, "they can still buy them from the Japanese or their 'quasi-agents'. But they can do so only at the pleasure of the Japanese."
This might be a modification of the Japanese firm's original plan, it was stated, but it amounted to the same thing. Foreign packers here will be reduced to the position of jobbers instead of wholesalers as originally the case and purchasers abroad would be required to pay, indirectly, a fee to the Japanese and their puppet regime although they are supposedly buying their supplies on a quota system.

Quota Plan Condemned
The quota system, it was pointed out, would virtually ban sales of eggs and egg products in Britain by Japanese since before the enactment of the law providing for the system. Japanese firms had only a very small share in the business. This system was said to have directly influenced the abandonment of the monopolistic plan of the Japanese.
A report printed by Wang Ching-wei's mouthpiece, Central China Daily News, on January 7, stated that it learned from well-informed business circles here that the "Shanghai Egg Merchants' Guild" would soon have complete control of the egg industry.

Must Ship To Hongkew
"All merchants who collected eggs from the interior," it stated, "will have to ship them to Hongkew and sell half of their collection to the Guild while the remaining half will be allowed to be sent to the south of the Soochow Creek."
"All merchants will pay ¥2 for one basket of eggs (one basket containing 750 eggs) to the Guild for the permit to collect eggs in the interior. Half of the permit fee will be returned to the merchant when half of the eggs collected is surrendered to the Guild in Hongkew."

《字林西报》。
日方称在华蛋品打包商将沦为中间商

作者：PAUL FENG

昨日流传的新闻报道声称，三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）已放弃其在中国庞大蛋品业务中的垄断计划，但此消息在本港消息灵通人士中未能得到证实。

一位蛋商对《字林西报》表示：“所谓日本人有意让鸡蛋自由通过长江三角洲运往上海的说法，远非事实。”

他指出，这并不意味着在沪的外国打包商无法获得货源。“如果他们愿意，”他说，“他们仍然可以从日本人或其‘准代理人’那里购买。但他们能否买到，完全取决于日本人的意愿。”

据称，这可能是该日本公司原计划的修改，但实质并无二致。在沪的外国打包商将从原本的批发商地位降格为中间商（jobbers），而海外的买家虽然表面上是按配额制度采购，实则需间接向日本人及其傀儡政权支付费用。

谴责配额制度

有人指出，配额制度实际上禁止了日本人在英国销售鸡蛋及蛋制品，因为在该制度相关法律颁布之前，日本公司在该业务中仅占极小份额。据说这一制度直接影响了日本人放弃其垄断计划。

汪精卫的喉舌《华中日报》于1月7日刊登的一篇报道 stated，该报从本港消息灵通的商界获悉，“上海蛋业公会”即将完全控制蛋品行业。

必须运往虹口

报道 stated：“所有从内地收集鸡蛋的商人，必须将鸡蛋运至虹口，并将所收鸡蛋的一半出售给公会，另一半则允许运往苏州河以南地区。”

“所有商人须向公会支付每篮鸡蛋2元（每篮含750枚鸡蛋）的费用，以获取在内地收集鸡蛋的许可证。当商人将在虹口收集的一半鸡蛋移交给公会时，一半的许可证费用将退还给商人。”

Egg Monopoly
Report Untrue

A flat denial that the Japanese firm of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha was now operating an egg monopoly, was issued yesterday by a Japanese Embassy spokesman here. The company instructed him that it had neither formed such a monopoly nor contemplated doing so, as reported by Chinese sources yesterday, he declared.

The spokesman said the prevailing misconception that such a monopoly existed was due to erroneous information.

Negotiations are now under way to secure permits for various firms to send their own buyers up country instead of making egg purchases through Japanese buyers as is the present practice, he said.

Transportation of eggs from the interior was subject to the permit system, he said and investigation into the validity of the permits has been the cause of difficulties in the past.

The spokesman added that he had been informed by Mitsui that all eggs allegedly stolen from various Shanghai firms had been returned to their owners and receipts for the return were in possession of the company.

Foreign egg packers yesterday expressed no surprise at the reported organization of a large Japanese combine, believed to be a subsidiary of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisen, to complete the Japanese plan of effecting a total monopoly of China's enormous egg trade.

Business At Standstill

While professing to have no details of the new organization, they stated that ever since last summer the number of eggs which they had been able to export into Shanghai for ex- port had been negligible.

Despite the Japanese promise that eggs would be allowed to go through under special permits issued by military authorities, it was revealed, packers here virtually had been forced to suspend operation.

Dealers Given Permits

A number of Chinese dealers here, according to information gathered by THE CHINA PRESS, had been permitted to ship eggs to Shanghai, but they were not eggs for the general market. Only with the permission of the Mitsui firm, it was learned, could the dealers dispose of any part of imports here.

These Chinese dealers were said to have been organized by the Japanese more than two months ago when foreign packers vigorously protested against the seizure of their eggs from the Yangtse delta and against discrimination aimed at them by the Japanese.

Peacetime Practice

It was learned that in peacetime, trade with foreign packers was widely solicited by these small dealers. The practice was that the foreigners would purchase from them all the eggs and egg products they could bring to Shanghai in addition to purchases made by their own agents in the producing areas.

Foreign packers stated, however, they had not given up the fight for equal trade privileges in the Yangtse delta. They expected some sort of showdown in the next two or three weeks.

Japanese quarters, however, denied the organization of a large combine which Chinese reports said had been named Cheng Hwa Company. The new firm was said to have come into existence on January 1.

《字林西报》。

日方称
鸡蛋垄断
报道不实

日本大使馆发言人昨日断然否认三井物产株式会社目前正在实行鸡蛋垄断。他宣称，该公司指示他声明，正如中方消息源昨日所报道的那样，该公司既未形成此类垄断，也未打算这样做。

该发言人表示，目前普遍存在的关于存在此类垄断的误解，是由于错误信息所致。

他说，目前正在进行谈判，以确保各公司能获得许可证，派遣自己的买家前往内地，而不是像目前做法那样通过日本买家购买鸡蛋。

他说，从内地运输鸡蛋受许可证制度约束，过去对许可证有效性的调查一直是造成困难的原因。

该发言人补充说，他已从三井方面获悉，据称从上海各公司窃走的所有鸡蛋均已归还给所有者，且公司持有归还收据。

昨日，外国鸡蛋打包商对于据报道组建了一个大型日本联合体（被认为是三井物产株式会社的子公司）以完成日本人彻底垄断中国庞大鸡蛋贸易计划的说法，并未表示惊讶。

业务停滞

尽管声称不了解新组织的细节，但他们表示，自去年夏天以来，他们能够出口到上海用于外销的鸡蛋数量微乎其微。

据悉，尽管日本人承诺凭军事当局颁发的特别许可证允许鸡蛋通行，但在沪的打包商实际上已被迫停止运营。

经销商获发许可证

据《字林西报》收集的信息，在沪的一些中国经销商已获准将鸡蛋运往上海，但这些鸡蛋并非供应一般市场。据了解，只有经过三井公司的许可，经销商才能处置任何部分进口至此的货物。

据说，这些中国经销商是在两个多月前由日本人组织起来的，当时外国打包商强烈抗议日本人在长江三角洲扣押他们的鸡蛋以及针对他们的歧视行为。

和平时期的做法

据了解，在和平时期，这些小经销商广泛招揽与外国打包商的贸易。当时的做法是，外国人除了由其代理人在产区采购外，还会从这些经销商处购买他们能运到上海的所有鸡蛋及蛋制品。

然而，外国打包商表示，他们并未放弃争取在长江三角洲享有平等贸易特权的斗争。他们预计在未来两三年内会有某种形式的摊牌。

然而，日方否认组建了一个大型联合体，中方报道曾称该联合体名为“成华公司”。据说这家新公司于1月1日成立。

“无鸡蛋垄断”

昨日否认
新公司成立

有关三井物产株式会社已成为一家子公司主要负责人的报道——该子公司旨在行使对中国鸡蛋贸易的日本垄断权——在日本大使馆发言人于昨日的日本记者招待会上予以否认。他表示，三井物产株式会社官员指出，报道中提及的那类公司并不存在。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
JAN 9 1940

Foreign Packers Hope For Free Yangtze Buying
Big Steal Repayments Not Completed By Japanese
BETTER DAYS SEEN AHEAD
Exposures By Evepost Aid In Checking Monopoly

The egg monopoly plans of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, who at one time intended to oust all other firms, including Japanese, from the Yangtze trade in this line, are going into the discard following decision by London that eggs can only be imported into Britain by permits based on a quota.

Decision for this quota, based on pre-hostilities shipping quotas, was taken six weeks ago. In this interval many things have happened behind the scenes, with the result that the Japanese embassy spokesman at yesterday's press conference flatly denied that the MBK was operating a monopoly.

Repayments Incomplete
Complete repayment for the eggs taken by the MBK from foreign firms in October and November, to the tune of over $500,000 has not been fully completed, despite a statement by the spokesman yesterday to the contrary. There are several necessary adjustments still outstanding.

Present indications are that free buying of eggs in the Yangtze delta may be allowed once more in the near future, and negotiations to that end are said to be making good progress. The snag at the moment is that military passes can only be issued to the Yangtze Egg Produce Company (alias MBK), but it has been arranged that third-party firms will given these by the MBK yet have the cargoes consigned in their own names.

MBK And CEPCO
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha before the hostilities was not in the egg export business, most of which went to Britain. The new London system of quotas was based on figures of pre-hostilities days, which would have meant that the MBK, with grandiose schemes to monopolize the market, would not have been able to send any of its eggs to Britain, now the only outlet.

The MBK, however, has taken over some 60 percent of the China Egg Produce Company, this being the figure represented by mortgages held by Chinese Government banks, the privilege being given MBK by the Japanese government. The Whangpoo Road premises were renamed for the Yangtze Egg Produce Company (alias MBK). Thus the MBK had taken over plant which had previously been represented in the egg export quotas arranged by the local Egg Conference.

Chance For MBK
Local third-party egg packers were not opposed to allowing the MBK into the import quotas arranged by London, and discussions have been going on for the past six weeks on this score. The foreign packers went into these discussions only on the basis that free buying of eggs be permitted in the future.

Demands by the MBK in this scheme were on the high side, as the Japanese firm wanted something like half of the trade. Cepco did just over a quarter in pre-hostility days. The third party packers however, have held firm, and it appears at present that conditions may possibly go back almost to pre-hostility levels, if present trends continue.

The Big Steal
MBK's big steal in October has not as yet been fully liquidated. Following the exposures made in the Shanghai Evening Post, MBK started replacing stolen cargoes with others of their own. Some of these, however, have not been up to standard, and the foreign packers' claims on behalf of these have not yet been paid in full.

Added to this, MBK took several cargoes consigned to American and British firms and paid these firms for them at their own valuations, which were below the actual cost price. The foreign firms are still pressing for adjustment of these figures.

1940年1月9日

外国打包商希望恢复长江流域自由采购
日方尚未完成大规模盗窃赔偿
前景看好
《晚邮报》的揭露有助于遏制垄断

三井物产株式会社的鸡蛋垄断计划正被搁置，该公司曾一度意图将所有其他公司（包括日本公司）排挤出该领域的长江贸易。此举紧随伦敦决定鸡蛋仅能凭基于配额的许可证进口到英国之后。

这项基于战前航运配额的配额决定是在六周前做出的。在此期间，幕后发生了许多事情，导致日本大使馆发言人在昨日的记者招待会上断然否认三井物产株式会社（MBK）正在实行垄断。

赔偿未完成

尽管发言人昨日发表了相反的声明，但三井物产株式会社在10月和11月从外国公司拿走的鸡蛋（价值超过50万美元）的全额赔偿尚未完全完成。仍有几项必要的调整尚未解决。

目前的迹象表明，不久后可能会再次允许在长江三角洲自由采购鸡蛋，据说为此进行的谈判进展顺利。目前的症结在于，军事通行证只能签发给长江蛋品公司（即三井物产株式会社的别名），但已安排由三井物产株式会社向第三方公司发放这些通行证，而货物则以第三方公司自己的名义托运。

三井物产株式会社与中国蛋品公司（CEPCO）

在敌对行动开始前，三井物产株式会社并未从事鸡蛋出口业务，大部分鸡蛋出口至英国。伦敦新的配额制度是基于战前的数据制定的，这意味着怀有垄断市场宏大计划的三井物产株式会社将无法将其任何鸡蛋送往英国，而英国现在是唯一的出口市场。

然而，三井物产株式会社已接管了中国蛋品公司（China Egg Produce Company）约60%的股份，这一比例由中国政府银行持有的抵押贷款代表，该特权由日本政府授予三井物产株式会社。黄浦路的原址已更名为长江蛋品公司（即三井物产株式会社的别名）。因此，三井物产株式会社接管了此前在当地鸡蛋会议安排的鸡蛋出口配额中占有份额的工厂。

三井物产株式会社的机会

当地第三方鸡蛋打包商并不反对允许三井物产株式会社进入由伦敦安排的进口配额，过去六周一直就此进行讨论。外国打包商参与这些讨论的前提是未来允许自由采购鸡蛋。

在此方案中，三井物产株式会社的要求偏高，因为这家日本公司想要大约一半的贸易份额。中国蛋品公司在战前仅占略高于四分之一的份额。然而，第三方打包商立场坚定，目前看来，如果当前趋势持续，条件可能会几乎恢复到战前水平。

大规模盗窃

三井物产株式会社在10月的大规模盗窃行为尚未完全清算。继《上海晚邮报》进行揭露后，三井物产株式会社开始用其自己的货物替换被盗货物。然而，其中一些货物不符合标准，外国打包商代表这些货物提出的索赔尚未得到全额支付。

此外，三井物产株式会社还拿走了几批运给美国和英国公司的货物，并按其自行评估的价值向这些公司付款，该价值低于实际成本价。外国公司仍在敦促调整这些数字。

January 9. 1940. Afternoon Translation

National Herald, Ta Ying Yeh Pao :-

JAPANESE MONOPOLIZE EGG TRADE

With a view to monopolizing the egg trade, the Japanese Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, Limited, has organized a new firm known as the Chen Hwa Company (成華洋行) to effect an extensive collection of eggs from the environs of Shanghai and the neighbouring suburban cities. Owing to this special influence, egg dealers are forced to sell the eggs at a reduced price. As this affects the business of the egg dealers and the livelihood of the poor hawkers, the egg dealers refuse to get eggs for the Japanese and the egg business in the neighbouring cities is brought to a standstill. Eggs secretly carried to Shanghai by poor hawkers for sale are searched out and confiscated by the Japanese.

It is learned that the Japanese Special Service Section has ordered the Shanghai City Government to instruct the administrative office in Pootung to prevent export of eggs from Pootung. A notice has been issued by the Pootung Administrative Office to the effect that eggs should only be sold to the Chen Hwa Company and that no export of eggs from Pootung was allowed.

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
1939
271-5

MBK Monopoly
Ousts Foreigners

Shanghai Packers Find
Trade Impossible
In New Plan

While the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha in the past few days has begun to replace the $500,000 worth of eggs it had stolen from two American and five British firms since October 10 last, it has at the same time completed a scheme of permits and pledges whereby third party packers will be excluded from the China market and MBK will have a monopoly unless third power diplomats act quickly.

This startling development in the background of the situation has been obscured by the Shanghai mass thefts, but a Shanghai Evening Post interview with one of the foreign firms shows that Admiral T C Hart was not completely informed when he said in Manila on Saturday that Tientsin for Americans was the only place where sometimes things had gone beyond the annoyance stage.

Taking All

For some time the Japanese firm of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha has resorted to the practice of taking possession of all egg shipments arriving in Shanghai, irrespective of ownership of the cargoes. British and American firms who are engaged in the egg packing trade, have suffered heavily, not only from having their eggs stolen, but from the restriction which such action places upon the normal conduct of the trade. Even if the eggs are not stolen on arrival, the system which has been worked up and is now in effect, makes it actually impossible for third-power packers to operate. Evepost is informed.

By virtue of the military control which the Japanese hold in occupied areas, the firm of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha by arrangement with the Japanese Army, has imposed such restrictions and conditions under which third-power packers can buy and transport eggs from Japanese occupied areas that the business of such third-power packers cannot be continued. The following will give an example of how the restrictions operate in order to give M.B.K. a monopoly of the industry:—

Ends Nowhere

The procedure necessary for third-power packers to buy and ship eggs from Chaohsien, Haowei, Wuhu, Anking, Pengpu, Chinkiang, Yangchow, Lungtan, Wiush and Changsha, is to go through a process which like the definition for a sphere of infinite radius, begins everywhere and ends nowhere. First of all, the services of a Japanese company or a Japanese individual must be secured for making application to the Japanese Egg Association for a so-called "removal permit". In making the application for a removal permit, said Japanese individual or firm must apply for a fixed number of baskets, which are desired for purchase in a certain district and the application must be accompanied by a payment of Yen 2 for every basket that is applied for.

Providing however, that the third-power packer makes a separate agreement with the Japanese Egg Association, that they will sell to M.B.K. on arrival of the eggs in Shanghai 50 percent of the total quantity purchased, at a price to be fixed by them at their discretion, the Japanese Egg Association will apply to the Asia Development Board for their signature to the removal permit. The person in charge of this particular work at the Asia Development Board is also an employee of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, and therefore actually the decision as to whether the permit is granted or not, rests with M.B.K. The time of expiration of these permits is limited, so often they expire before eggs can be purchased and shipped. In that event a further procedure has to be gone through in order to get additional permits or a renewal of the permits, and the time ensued often results in the spoilage of the eggs or a good percentage of them.

Sell At Loss

Assuming therefore that a third-power packer should agree to sell 50 percent of the eggs purchased to M.B.K. at the price which it decides to pay for them and that said eggs arrive in Shanghai, M.B.K. would take possession of all the eggs shipped. Then according to agreement, M.B.K. retained 50 percent of the eggs that third-power packers have purchased and brought in, for which they are to accept the price which M.B.K. decides to fix on these eggs. In the past on stolen cargo, the price which M.B.K. has been willing to pay for such eggs taken, would range about $20 per 100 lbs. less than the actual cost of the eggs.

It is well to keep in mind that in order to purchase eggs at the ports mentioned above, the actual cash must be sent to these places in order to buy the eggs. Consequently a third power packer must finance the egg purchasing in the country at his own risk; only receiving 50 percent of the eggs thus purchased when they arrive in Shanghai, and accept a price from M.B.K., for the other 50 percent considerably below the actual value of the eggs. Furthermore on the 50 percent of the eggs that the third-power packer is to receive, he must pay M.B.K. 50 sen per basket commission before he can take delivery. It is quite easy to see therefore, that under this system it is actually impossible for a third-power packer to purchase and ship eggs from the above-mentioned ports.

Kompoh System

A little different system applies to the Kompoh district (Kiangsu province north of the Yangtze River) and applying to shipping points such as Hsinkong, Changwangkong and Hsin Hsinkong. In order to be able to ship eggs from these ports which must be shipped on Japanese steamers as no other steamers are available, it is necessary for representatives of third-power packers at these shipping points to sign the following pledge: This is a translation of the pledge which is written in Japanese:—

"To the Shanghai Branch of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.
We hereby pledge that the... baskets of hen eggs we shipped to Shanghai today, will be delivered to your company on arrival without fail, and we agree to their being paid according to the price fixed by the Japanese Egg Association.

Egg Company
on the ... day of ... month of the 14th year of Showa."

MBK Sets Price

Consequently buying eggs from the whole Kompoh district and shipping from a port there, a pledge must be signed that all of the eggs shipped will be delivered to Mitsui Bussan Kaisha on arrival in Shanghai and that the price which it offers for the eggs, will be accepted. The pledge states that the price would be fixed by the Japanese Egg Association, but as this Association is completely under the control of M.B.K., it amounts to the same thing.

A little different arrangement applies at Taichow. A Japanese lawyer has formed a transportation company at this point, which is the only transportation company there, and in order to transport eggs from this point, foreign packers must pay him Yen 3 per basket in order to secure a pass to transport the eggs to Shanghai.

Third Powers Excluded

From this it is obvious that it is impossible to buy eggs from any point where eggs are available and it shows very definitely that means have now been worked out whereby third-power packers are definitely prevented from securing and shipping eggs.

Mitsui Bussan Kaisha therefore, through the assistance of the Japanese Army, has created an effective monopoly whereby if no changes can be made in the general system of purchasing eggs, all third-power packers have been eliminated from the egg industry in Central China Evepost's informant concluded.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。
1939年
271-5

三井物产垄断
排挤外商

上海蛋商发现
在新计划下
贸易无法进行

尽管三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）近日已开始赔偿自去年10月10日以来从两家美国公司和五家英国公司窃取的总值50万美元的鸡蛋，但与此同时，它已完成了一项许可证与保证书计划，据此将把第三方包装商排除在中国市场之外，除非第三国外交官迅速采取行动，否则三井物产株式会社（MBK）将形成垄断。

这一发生在背景中的惊人事态被上海的大规模盗窃案所掩盖，但《上海晚邮报》对一家外国公司的采访显示，当哈特（T. C. Hart）海军上将周六在马尼拉称天津是对于美国人而言有时事态已超出滋扰阶段的唯一地方时，他并未完全掌握情况。

全部攫取

一段时间以来，日本公司三井物产株式会社一直采取扣押所有抵达上海的鸡蛋货运的做法，无论货物所有权归属如何。从事鸡蛋包装贸易的英美公司遭受了严重损失，不仅因为鸡蛋被盗，还因为这种行为对正常贸易活动造成了限制。《晚邮报》获悉，即使鸡蛋在抵达时未被窃取，目前已建立并生效的制度也使得第三方包装商实际上无法运营。

凭借日军在占领区的军事控制，三井物产株式会社通过与日本陆军的安排，实施了诸多限制和条件，使得第三方包装商从日占区购买和运输鸡蛋变得不可能，从而导致此类第三方包装商的生意无法继续。以下将举例说明这些限制如何运作，以使三井物产株式会社（M.B.K.）垄断该行业：—

永无终点

第三方包装商从巢县、好微（音译）、芜湖、安庆、蚌埠、镇江、扬州、龙潭、维什（音译）和长沙购买并装运鸡蛋所需的程序，是一个如同无限半径球体定义般的过程，始于各处而终于虚无。首先，必须聘请一家日本公司或一名日本人向日本鸡蛋协会申请所谓的“移出许可证”。在申请移出许可证时，该日本个人或公司必须申请在特定地区购买固定数量的篮筐，并且每申请一篮需随附支付2日元。

然而，如果第三方包装商与日本鸡蛋协会达成单独协议，承诺在鸡蛋抵达上海时将其购买总量的50%出售给三井物产株式会社（M.B.K.），价格由后者自行决定，那么日本鸡蛋协会将向亚洲开发委员会申请签署移出许可证。亚洲开发委员会负责此项具体工作的人员也是三井物产株式会社的雇员，因此实际上是否颁发许可证的决定权掌握在三井物产株式会社手中。这些许可证的有效期有限，因此往往在鸡蛋能够购买和装运之前就已过期。在这种情况下，必须经过进一步的程序以获得额外许可证或续期，而由此耗费的时间往往导致鸡蛋或部分鸡蛋变质。

亏本出售

因此，假设第三方包装商同意以三井物产株式会社决定的价格向其出售所购鸡蛋的50%，且所述鸡蛋抵达上海，三井物产株式会社将接管所有装运的鸡蛋。然后根据协议，三井物产株式会社扣留第三方包装商购买并运入的鸡蛋的50%，对此第三方包装商必须接受三井物产株式会社对这些鸡蛋定的价格。过去对于被盗货物，三井物产株式会社愿意为这些被拿走的鸡蛋支付的价格，大约比鸡蛋的实际成本每100磅低20美元。

值得注意的是，为了在上述港口购买鸡蛋，必须将现金实际汇往这些地方以购买鸡蛋。因此，第三方包装商必须自行承担风险在内陆资助鸡蛋采购；当鸡蛋抵达上海时，仅能收到所购鸡蛋的50%，并接受三井物产株式会社为另外50%鸡蛋制定的远低于其实际价值的价格。此外，对于第三方包装商将收到的那50%鸡蛋，他在提货前必须向三井物产株式会社支付每篮50钱（sen）的佣金。因此不难看出，在这种制度下，第三方包装商实际上不可能从上述港口购买和装运鸡蛋。

通港（Kompoh）体系

通港地区（江苏省长江以北地区）适用一种稍有不同的体系，适用于新港、张王港和新新港等装运点。为了能够从这些港口装运鸡蛋（由于没有其他轮船可用，必须使用日本轮船），第三方包装商在这些装运点的代表必须签署以下保证书：以下是用日文写成的保证书的译文：—

“致三井物产株式会社上海分公司。
我们特此保证，我们今天装运至上海的……篮鲜鸡蛋，将在抵达时无误地交付给贵公司，并同意按照日本鸡蛋协会确定的价格进行结算。

鸡蛋公司
于昭和14年……月……日。”

三井物产定价

因此，从整个通港地区购买鸡蛋并从那里港口装运，必须签署一份保证书，承诺所有装运的鸡蛋在抵达上海时将交付给三井物产株式会社，并接受其提供的鸡蛋价格。保证书称价格将由日本鸡蛋协会确定，但由于该协会完全受三井物产株式会社（M.B.K.）控制，这实际上是同一回事。

泰州适用一种稍有不同的安排。一名日本律师在此地成立了一家运输公司，这是当地唯一的运输公司，为了从此地运输鸡蛋，外国包装商必须向他支付每篮3日元，以获得将鸡蛋运往上海的通行证。

排除第三方

由此可见，从任何有鸡蛋供应的地方购买鸡蛋都是不可能的，这也非常明确地表明，现在已经制定出各种手段，确凿地阻止第三方包装商获取和装运鸡蛋。

《晚邮报》的消息人士总结道，因此，三井物产株式会社在日本陆军的协助下，建立了一种有效的垄断，如果鸡蛋采购的总体制度不能改变，所有第三方包装商都将被排除出华中地区的鸡蛋行业。

Seven Arrested
Chinese Given
Court Release

Rue Delastre Company
Allowed To Take
Hundred Tons

RIVER POLICE
SOLVE THEFTS

$500,000 Racket Case
In Huge Swindle
Continuing

Creating a sensation in local crime and court history, the Mitsui Busan, Kaisha, widely-publicized Japanese firm within the past few months for its thefts of eggs purchased by foreign concerns, refused to prosecute seven coal-thieves brought before the Second Special District Court after arrest by the Customs River Police for stealing more than 100 tons of Tsingtao coal from the MBK coalyards in Pootung.

It was revealed in testimony presented before Judge Soong of the Second Special District Court that the seven coal-thieves brought before the court were in addition to eight others already apprehended by the police, and had participated in a major misappropriation of coal from the MBK yards in Pootung only last Tuesday.

Men Released

Despite the evidence offered by a member of the Customs River police that the stolen coal had been recovered from the seven men standing in the court's dock, Judge Soong declared at the conclusion of the hearing that he was reluctantly compelled to order the release of the men owing to the fact that the owners of the coal had refused to prosecute the case.

The Customs River Police, it was disclosed at the court hearing, possessed an "air-tight" case against the seven accused, and had arrested the men with a large quantity of coal in their possession, the arrest leading to further discovery of a 100-ton "hill" of coal in the yards of the Teh Woo Coal Company at 155 Route Delastre.

Inside Job

As a result of the arrest of the seven men, however, police were able to ascertain that the thefts of more than $500,000 worth of coal from the Kailan Mining Administration, Shanghai Power Company, Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and Nee Tai Shing Coal Hong within the past five months, were all carefully planned with "inside" assistance.

A detective of the Pootung Point River Police, was the principal witness featured at the hearing brought against the seven coal-theft suspects.

Modus Operandi

The River Police official described the daring manner in which the coal-thieves had operated Tuesday's robbery from the MBK coalyard, and revealed the subsequent manner in which a large quantity of the stolen property had been discovered at the Teh Woo Coal Company at 155 Route Delastre.

According to the testimony of the detective, an ordinary lighter tried up alongside the MBK coalyards in Pootung shortly before noon on Tuesday, and its crew requested delivery of 37 tons of coal for which payment had already been made to the MBK office in Shanghai and for which a delivery order had been issued.

Passes Switched

Owing to the hour, however the MBK wharf manager refused to make delivery and ordered the cargo-boat to return at 2 p.m. As soon as the manager's "back was turned," another lighter appeared on the scene, and the license number of the first boat and crew passes were transferred to the second lighter.

The latter boat, it was revealed in the evidence, took the place of the first lighter and succeeded in loading more than 27 tons of coal before 2 p.m., when it withdrew from the scene and again transferred the license and passes of the crew to the first lighter.

Presented Again

Upon the reappearance of the MBK coalyard manager, the first lighter again presented the bill of removal for 37 tons of coal, and this was readily permitted by the manager, thus making it a total of 64 tons of coal obtained by the coal-thieves instead of the 37 tons contained in the genuine order form.

A River Police search party, especially on the look-out for coal-thieves, spotted the second lighter entering the Soochow Creek, and after watching its suspicious movements, traced the unloading of coal from the lighter onto an awaiting truck at Chapoo Road Bridge, which then led the investigators to the Teh Woo Coal Hong on Route Delastre, where a further amount of nearly 100 tons of stolen coal was discovered.

Tsingtao Coal

It was disclosed in court that an official of the MBK was informed of the investigations carried out by the River Police, and after being shown a sample of the coal recovered from the thieves, identified it as "Tsingtao coal" and only shipped into Shanghai by the MBK.

Following this the MBK official was led to the Teh Woo Coal Hong on Route Delastre and there shown more than 100 tons of the same quality coal piled up at the rear of the coalyard. On this occasion the MBK's representative was accompanied by a member of the French Concession police, besides members of the River Police, and in their presence identified the stolen property as the MBK's Tsingtao coal.

No Prosecution

Despite all these facts, however, the court was informed that the MBK had refused to prosecute the seven men arrested by the River Police, and in view of this Judge Soong declared that he had no other alternative but to order the seven men to be freed from custody.

Attempting to obtain further information on the case, the Evening Post learned from reliable sources that one of the chief reasons for the MBK's failure to launch proceedings against the seven men was due to a fear that evidence would reveal that the stolen coal had been misappropriated from the company by some of its own Japanese staff members.

Chinese Court

Apart from this, the possibility was held that the Japanese concern did not feel favorable toward dealing with a Chinese court governed by the Chungking regime.

As a result of the MBK's refusal to continue proceedings in the case, the stolen coal held by the Teh Woo Coal Hong was ordered to be released again to the hong, and members of the French Concession police, who have been guarding the coal since Tuesday, were removed from the coalyard this morning.

Police Victory

A high police official told the Evening Post this morning that, despite the withdrawal of the case, it could be considered a major victory for the police, supporting all earlier belief that coal stolen within recent months from the large coal importing hongs in the city had been "inside jobs."

This, the police official declared, was a significantly different thing to the petty larceny committed by ordinary wharf thieves, as the thefts from such companies as the Kailan Mining Administration, Shanghai Power Company, Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and Nee Tai Shing Coal Hong amounted to more than 10,000 tons each month, and had caused a total loss to the companies within the past five months of well over $500,000.

七人被捕
华人获
法庭释放

德拉司脱路公司
获准提取
百吨煤炭

水上警察
破获盗窃案

五十万美元敲诈案
涉及巨额诈骗
仍在继续

三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）这家日本公司在过去几个月因窃取外商购买的鸡蛋而广受关注，其在当地犯罪和法庭历史上引起了轰动。该公司拒绝起诉七名窃煤贼，这些人在被海关水上警察逮捕后，被带至第二特区法院受审，罪名是从浦东的英商开平矿务局（MBK）煤场窃取一百多吨青岛煤。

在第二特区法院宋法官（Judge Soong）面前提供的证词显示，被带上法庭的七名窃煤贼之外，另有八人已被警方抓获，他们参与了仅在上周二发生的从浦东英商开平矿务局煤场大规模盗用煤炭的案件。

人员获释

尽管海关水上警察的一名成员提供证据称，从站在被告席上的七人那里追回了被盗煤炭，但宋法官在听证会结束时宣布，由于煤炭所有者拒绝起诉此案，他不得不勉强命令释放这些人。

据法庭听证会披露，海关水上警察掌握了针对这七名被告“无懈可击”的证据，并在逮捕时查获了他们持有的大量煤炭，此次逮捕还导致进一步发现了位于德拉司脱路（Route Delastre）155号德和煤行（Teh Woo Coal Company）堆场内的一百吨“煤山”。

内部作案

然而，由于这七人的被捕，警方得以查明，在过去五个月内，从开平矿务局、上海电力公司、三井物产株式会社以及尼泰盛煤号（Nee Tai Shing Coal Hong）窃取的总值超过50万美元的煤炭，均是在“内部”协助下精心策划的。

浦东角水上警察局的一名侦探是此次针对七名窃煤嫌疑人的听证会上的主要证人。

作案手法

这位水上警察官员描述了窃煤贼在周二从英商开平矿务局煤场实施抢劫的大胆方式，并揭示了随后在德拉司脱路155号德和煤行发现大量赃物的经过。

根据该侦探的证词，周二临近中午时，一艘普通驳船靠上了浦东英商开平矿务局的煤场，其船员要求交付37吨煤炭，声称已向英商开平矿务局上海办事处付款并已取得提货单。

调换通行证

然而，由于时间关系，英商开平矿务局的码头经理拒绝交货，并命令货船于下午2点返回。一旦经理“转身离开”，另一艘驳船便出现在现场，第一艘船的牌照号码和船员通行证被转移到了第二艘驳船上。

证据显示，后一艘船取代了第一艘驳船的位置，并在下午2点前成功装载了超过27吨煤炭，随后撤离现场，再次将牌照和船员通行证转回给第一艘驳船。

再次出示单据

当英商开平矿务局煤场经理再次出现时，第一艘驳船再次出示了37吨煤炭的提货单，经理轻易地予以放行，从而使窃煤贼获得的煤炭总量达到64吨，而非真实订单中包含的37吨。

一支专门搜寻窃煤贼的水上警察搜查队，发现第二艘驳船进入苏州河，在监视其可疑举动后，追踪到该驳船在乍浦路桥将煤炭卸到一辆等候的卡车上，这引导调查人员来到德拉司脱路的德和煤行，在那里又发现了近100吨被盗煤炭。

青岛煤

法庭披露，英商开平矿务局的一名官员获悉了水上警察进行的调查，在查看了从窃贼处缴获的煤炭样本后，确认其为“青岛煤”，且仅由英商开平矿务局运入上海。

随后，该英商开平矿务局官员被带到德拉司脱路的德和煤行，并向其展示了堆放在煤场后部的100多吨同品质煤炭。此次，英商开平矿务局的代表除水上警察成员外，还有一名法租界警察陪同，并在他们面前指认被盗物品为英商开平矿务局的青岛煤。

不予起诉

尽管有上述事实，但法庭获悉，英商开平矿务局拒绝起诉被水上警察逮捕的七人，鉴于此，宋法官宣布他别无选择，只能命令释放这七人。

《晚邮报》试图从可靠消息来源获取有关此案的更多信息，得知英商开平矿务局未对这七人提起诉讼的主要原因之一，是担心证据会揭示被盗煤炭是被其内部的一些日本职员盗用的。

中国法院

此外，还有一种可能性，即这家日本公司不愿在与重庆国民政府管辖下的中国法院打交道。

由于英商开平矿务局拒绝继续推进此案，当局命令将德和煤行持有的被盗煤炭再次释放给该煤行，自周二以来一直看守煤炭的法租界警察成员于今晨撤出煤场。

警方的胜利

一位高级警务官员今晨告诉《晚邮报》，尽管此案已撤销，但这仍可被视为警方的重大胜利，证实了此前所有的看法，即最近几个月从本市大型进口煤行窃取的煤炭均为“内部作案”。

这位警务官员宣称，这与普通码头小偷犯下的小偷小摸截然不同，因为从开平矿务局、上海电力公司、三井物产株式会社和尼泰盛煤行等公司窃取的煤炭每月超过10,000吨，在过去五个月内给各公司造成的总损失远超50万美元。

外人关切

这位警务官员强调，大规模煤炭抢劫是由一个“团伙”操作的，该团伙——

Packers Paying
MBK 'Yegg' Tax

Replacement Of Stolen
Cargoes Started
By Japanese

Making an effort to join the
ranks of reformed sinners, the
egoistic Mitsui Bussan Kaisha has
started to replace over 5000 bas-
kets of eggs stolen from two Ameri-
can and five British firms since
October 10. But they are still
acting as 'yeggs' in charging a
commission on new cargoes
brought in by these firms.
The MBK have not as yet tried
to charge a commission on the
replacements they are making,
which have amounted to several
hundred baskets in the past two
or three days. But the additional
charges made on the present ship-
ments to the third party firms
adds about $4 to the approximate-
ly $80 cost of 100 lb. of eggs.
Permit System
For the past year third party
firms have had to purchase per-
mits to buy eggs, at the rate of
Yen 2 per basket. These permits
have been issued at shipping
points. But some of the present
shipping points have no
mechanism to issue permits, with
the result that these cargoes ar-
rive in Shanghai without them.
And for these cargoes the Mitsui
Bussan Kaisha collects the Yen 2
per basket.
In addition, the MBK collects a
transport fee for the cargoes, pos-
sibly on behalf of the transport
organization, although foreign
packers cannot see what on earth
the MBK has to do with cargoes
which don't belong to it. In ad-
dition, the charge of 50 or 60 cents
per basket is made, against the
five to 10 cent cost estimated by
the seven firms.
Fifty Sen Squeeze
These cargoes without permits
are taken to the MBK's plant,
and released from this to the
third party firms. On the strength
of this the MBK charge 50 sen
squeeze per basket, ostensibly a
charge for release of the cargoes.
In other words, the MBK is mak-
ing on this count alone a 50 sen
per basket commission on business
of rival firms.
The third party firms have been
paying this squeeze, although
under protest as there is no
justification for it. But it has
been a question of possibly get-
ting some eggs, instead of none
at all. Shipments are once more
being released to their proper
consignees, and a start has been
made in the replacing of the $600,-
000 worth of stolen cargoes.
Open Door Policy
Third party packers are now
trying to get rid of this commis-
sion racket, which, they point out,
does not fit in with the Open Door
policy which the Japanese say
they are maintaining.
A lot has been done to clear up
the egg situation, thanks to pub-
lic indignation over the barefaced
manner, exposed by the Shanghai
Evening Post, in which the at-
tempt to kill foreign business was
made, and Japanese official reac-
tion. Packers will not be satisfied
until all their stolen eggs are
replaced and all the illegal charges
wiped out.

包装商支付
英商开平矿务局“惯窃”税

日本人开始
替换被盗货物

自私的三井物产株式会社正努力加入改过自新者的行列，已开始替换自10月10日以来从两家美国公司和五家英国公司窃取的5000多筐鸡蛋。但他们仍然像“惯窃”一样，对这些公司运进的新货物收取佣金。
英商开平矿务局尚未尝试对其正在进行的替换货物收取佣金，过去两三天内替换的数量已达数百筐。但是，对现运往第三方公司的货物加收的费用，使每100磅鸡蛋约80美元的成本增加了约4美元。
许可证制度
在过去一年里，第三方公司必须以每筐2日元的价格购买购买鸡蛋的许可证。这些许可证在装运点签发。但目前一些装运点没有签发许可证的机制，导致这些货物在没有许可证的情况下抵达上海。对于这些货物，三井物产株式会社收取每筐2日元的费用。
此外，英商开平矿务局还收取货物的运输费，可能是代表运输组织收取，尽管外国包装商看不出英商开平矿务局究竟与不属于它的货物有何关系。此外，每筐收取50或60美分的费用，而七家公司估计的成本仅为5到10美分。
五十钱压榨
这些没有许可证的货物被带到英商开平矿务局的工厂，并从那里放行给第三方公司。凭借这一点，英商开平矿务局每筐收取50钱的“压榨费”，名义上是放行货物的费用。换句话说，仅就这一项而言，英商开平矿务局就在竞争对手的业务中赚取每筐50钱的佣金。
第三方公司一直在支付这笔压榨费，虽然是出于抗议，因为没有正当理由。但这关系到是否能得到一些鸡蛋，而不是完全得不到。货物再次被放行给其合法的收货人，替换价值60万美元的被盗货物的工作已经开始。
门户开放政策
第三方包装商现在正试图摆脱这种佣金敲诈，他们指出，这与日本人声称维持的“门户开放”政策不符。
由于公众对《上海晚邮报》揭露的这种扼杀外商业务的厚颜无耻的方式感到愤怒，以及日本官方的反应，鸡蛋局势已得到很大程度的清理。包装商在所有被盗鸡蛋得到替换且所有非法收费被取消之前，不会感到满意。

No Settlement
With MBK, Say
Egg Concerns

Foreign egg purchasing houses
here will not come to any truce with
the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha for
settling the dispute arising from
theft of egg shipments by the
Japanese firm, until the latter
consents to fair treatment for all
competitors in the business, an
American company told THE CHINA
PRESS yesterday.

stated that the various British and
American firms are in constant in-
formal contact with each other and
are determined to face the mono-
poly seeking Japanese firm with a
united front. He flatly denied the
rumor that the British firms had
come to a marketing agreement
with the M.B.K.

This rumor was also denied by a
British firm, a spokesman of which
pointed out that most of the British
principals were in London and were
so incensed at the high-handed
methods of the Japanese company

tempt a settlement with it but want-

straightened through diplomatic

present situation in which up-

foreign firms are forcibly consign-

small Japanese firms which former-

to the American official quoted
above. He added that there are
about 4,000 baskets belonging to
various concerns here, now being

蛋业公司称
不与英商开平矿务局
达成和解

本地一家美国公司昨日告诉《字林西报》，在此家日本公司同意对所有商业竞争对手给予公平待遇之前，在沪的外国鸡蛋采购行不会与三井物产株式会社就因该日本公司盗窃鸡蛋货物而引起的纠纷达成任何休战协议。

该公司发言人表示，各家英美公司之间保持着不断的非正式接触，并决心以统一的阵线面对寻求垄断的日本公司。他断然否认了英国公司已与三井物产株式会社（M.B.K.）达成营销协议的谣言。

一家英国公司也否认了这一谣言，其发言人指出，大多数英方负责人均在伦敦，他们对这家日本公司的高压手段感到极为愤怒，因此不愿尝试与其达成和解，而是希望等待此事通过东京的外交渠道得到解决。

“Better To Talk Of Legs Than
Eggs”---Suma
Question
Evaded
Protest On MBK Theft
Declared Unknown
By Spokesman
“Better talk about legs,
than eggs,” Mr. Y. Suma,
spokesman of the Japanese
Foreign Office, laughingly
remarked to an assemblage
of 30 local and foreign news-
men, when interviewed by
them in the Broadway Man-
sions yesterday evening, fol-
lowing his arrival from Tokyo
by plane, on the first hop of a
special observation trip of
Japanese-occupied areas in China.
For nearly an hour and a half,
newsmen barraged Mr. Suma with
questions on the early formation
of Central Government in China,
possibilities of a Japan-Soviet non-
aggression pact, a new trade treaty
between Japan and the United
States, the “New Order In East
Asia,” etc., until the Giamusho
spokesman obtained respite from
the verbal onslaughts of the news-
papermen when he was asked to
comment on the recent exposures
of the methods by which the
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha deprived the
foreign concerns of eggs purchased
in the interior.
• Question Dodged
Mr. Suma did not reply to this
question as the interpreter point-
ed out that the Gaimusho spokes-
man had only arrived in Shanghai
a few hours before the conference.
The question was then directed
to Mr. Ken Tsurumi, spokesman
of the Japanese Embassy here.
Mr. Tsurumi stated that the MBK
denied any knowledge of the
allegations brought against it.
“Legal Issue”
Following the reply, one of the
correspondents pointed out the
procedure which was stated by for-
eign egg concerns to have been
used by the MBK in obtaining
eggs originally purchased by the
foreign plants. The correspondent
explained that bills of lading were
signed in which the MBK demand-
ed in having their name attached
as consignees.
No reply was made to the ques-
tion, and the correspondent again
asked whether it had become
possible for a private firm to seize
cargo belonging to another private
company.
The spokesman then answered
that the egg problem concerned a
legal issue.
Unaware Of Protests

enquired whether this statement
had been made to the protests
lodged by the British and Amer-
ican consulates.
“The spokesman is not aware
that protests have been made in
the matter.”
Mr. Suma then interrupted the
discussions and declared that it
was “better to talk about legs than
eggs.”
With that remark, newsmen ad-
journed further questions on the
egg problem until this afternoon’s
usual press conference.

“谈腿比谈蛋好”——须磨
回避提问
宣称不知晓关于三井物产盗窃案的抗议
发言人称

“还是谈谈腿，别谈蛋了，”日本外务省发言人须磨弥吉郎（Y. Suma）先生笑着对三十名中外记者说道。昨晚，他在从东京乘飞机抵达上海后，于百老汇大厦接受了记者们的采访，此次行程是他对中国日军占领区进行特别视察的第一站。

在一个半小时的时间里，记者们向须磨先生连珠炮般地提出了一系列问题，涉及中国中央政府的早期组建、日苏互不侵犯条约的可能性、美日新贸易条约、“东亚新秩序”等，直到这位外务省发言人在被要求就近期曝光的三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）剥夺外商在内地所购鸡蛋的手段一事发表评论时，才从记者们的言语围攻中获得喘息之机。

• 回避问题

须磨先生没有回答这个问题，因为翻译指出，外务省发言人在记者会开始前几小时才刚刚抵达上海。随后，问题转向了日本驻沪大使馆发言人鹤见健（Ken Tsurumi）先生。鹤见先生表示，三井物产株式会社否认对其提出的任何指控知情。

“法律问题”

在得到答复后，一名记者指出了外国蛋商所称的三井物产株式会社在获取原本由外资工厂购买的鸡蛋时所采用的程序。该记者解释说，在签署的提单中，三井物产株式会社要求将其名字列为收货人。

对此问题未作答复，该记者再次询问，私人公司是否已经有可能扣押属于另一家私人公司的货物。

发言人随后回答说，鸡蛋问题涉及一个法律问题。

不知晓抗议活动

另一名记者随即询问，这一声明是否针对英国和美国领事馆提出的抗议而作出。

“发言人并不知晓此事已提出抗议。”

须磨先生随后打断了讨论，并宣称“谈腿比谈蛋好”。

随着这句话，记者们暂停了关于鸡蛋问题的进一步提问，留待今天下午的例行记者招待会上再议。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

NOV 16 1939

British Journal
On “Egg Scandal”

Mitsui Bussan Kaisha
Party to Theft ; Loss
To British Firms

Under the heading “The Egg
Scandal,” the current issue of the
British Chamber of Commerce
Journal, which appears today, criticizes
the actions of the Japanese authori-
ties in taking possession of eggs
consigned to British and American
firms in Shanghai and placing them
under the control of the Mitsui
Bussan Kaisha, which firm, the
journal states, presumably had the
authority of the Japanese Govern-
ment to take possession of all eggs, re-
gardless of ownership, arriving at the
port. The article brands the action
of this firm as illegal and adds that
it is surprising that the premier
Japanese firm in the city should be a
party to what is nothing less than
theft.

The article is as follows: In total
disregard of all the assurances given
by Japanese spokesmen and officials,
Civil Military and Naval that the
interests of Third Power nationals
would be respected, large quantities
of eggs the property of British and
American owners have since early
October been taken by Japanese and
delivered to the Shanghai Trust &
Warehouse Co., and the Yangtze
Produce & Cold Storage Co.

Government Authority

Both these plants in which the eggs
are processed are under the control
of Messrs. Mitsui Bussan Kaisha
which firm presumably had the au-
thority of the Japanese Government
to take possession of all eggs, regard-
less of ownership, arriving at the
port.

Owing to the monopolization by the
Japanese of water transport in the
Yangtze delta, shipments of eggs can
be made on Japanese vessels only,
thereby facilitating their seizure, for
though the consignees hold bill of
lading made out in their name, such
shipping documents have been dis-
regarded, the eggs being handed over
to those who had no title to them.

It was thought that the strong re-
presentations that had been made in
regard to the purchasing of the eggs
had been effective, as for a few days
deliveries were not interfered with
but now—November 6—further mis-
appropriation of eggs on arrival, the
property of British firms has been
notified.

Foreign Property

It must be emphasized that the
eggs are the property of the British
and American firms concerned hav-
ing been bought and paid for by
them; that the firms concerned re-
quired the eggs for processing and
shipment abroad, mainly to Great
Britain, that the seizure of the eggs
seriously affects their interests and
if further seizures are countenanced
and condoned by the authorities will
render their plants inoperative; that
the seizure of the eggs prevents their
completing contracts into which they
had entered and renders them liable
to penalties. While all these points
are important the most serious aspects
of the whole matter are that no re-
liance can be placed on Japanese
assurances and that confidence can no
longer be placed in the security of
bills of lading issued by Japanese
shipping houses.

It is surprising that a firm of the
standing of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha,
the premier Japanese firm, should be
a party to what is nothing less than
theft, for the eggs have been removed
to premises under the control of the
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha without the
consent or approval of the owners.

Illegal

This attempt by illegal and grossly
unethical means to prevent supplies
reaching old established British, and
American egg packing plants and
presumably with the intention of
establishing a Japanese monopoly
cannot be too strongly condemned
and even though the present practice
be discontinued and full reparation
made for offence against common law
to say nothing of commercial moral-
ity, the whole must inevitably give
justification for scepticism.

Between October 14 and October 25
shipments to one British firm only
amounting to 2,337 baskets of eggs
valued at approximately C.N.$150,000
were seized and removed without
their authority to the Japanese con-
trolled plants above mentioned. Bills
of lading for these shipments are still
in possession of the British con-
signees.

When questioned by a “North-China
Daily News” reporter in connection
with the article an official of the
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha stated that his
firm had no statement to make. The
matter, he said, was in the hands of
the company’s lawyers.

《字林西报》

1939年11月16日

英国期刊
评“鸡蛋丑闻”

三井物产株式会社
参与盗窃；英商
遭受损失

在今日出版的英国商会期刊最新一期中，以“鸡蛋丑闻”为标题的文章批评了日本当局的行为，即没收运抵上海并 consign（委托/托运）给英美公司的鸡蛋，并将其置于三井物产株式会社的控制之下。该期刊称，该公司据称拥有日本政府的授权，可以没收所有抵达港口的鸡蛋，无论其所有权归属如何。文章将该公司的行为定性为非法，并补充说，令人惊讶的是，上海首屈一指的日本公司竟然参与了这无异于盗窃的行为。

文章内容如下：完全无视日本陆海空军政发言人和官员所作的一切保证——即尊重第三国国民的利益——自十月初以来，大量属于英美业主的鸡蛋被日本人拿走，并交付给上海信托仓库公司（Shanghai Trust & Warehouse Co.）和扬子冷藏公司（Yangtze Produce & Cold Storage Co.）。

政府授权

这两家加工鸡蛋的工厂均受三井物产株式会社控制，该公司据称拥有日本政府的授权，可以没收所有抵达港口的鸡蛋，无论其所有权归属如何。

由于日本人垄断了长江三角洲的水上运输，鸡蛋只能通过日本船只运输，从而便于其扣押。尽管收货人持有以其名义开具的提单，但这些运输单据被置之不理，鸡蛋被移交给无权占有者。

人们曾认为，此前就鸡蛋采购问题提出的强烈交涉已经生效，因为在几天内交货未受干扰，但现在——11月6日——又接到通知，属于英国公司的鸡蛋在抵达时再次被挪用。

外国财产

必须强调的是，这些鸡蛋是相关英美公司的财产，由他们购买并付款；相关公司需要这些鸡蛋用于加工并运往国外，主要是运往英国；扣押鸡蛋严重影响了他们的利益，如果当局继续纵容和默许进一步的扣押，将导致他们的工厂无法运营；扣押鸡蛋使他们无法完成已签订的合同，并使他们面临罚款风险。虽然所有这些点都很重要，但整个事件最严重的方面在于，日本的保证不可信赖，且不再能相信日本航运公司签发的提单的安全性。

令人惊讶的是，像三井物产株式会社这样地位显赫的日本头号公司，竟然参与了这无异于盗窃的行为，因为鸡蛋在未经所有者同意或批准的情况下，被移至三井物产株式会社控制的场所。

非法

这种试图通过非法和极不道德的手段阻止物资供应到达历史悠久的英美鸡蛋包装厂的行为，据推测其意图是建立日本垄断，对此怎么谴责都不为过。即使目前的做法停止，并对违反普通法的行为做出充分赔偿，更不用说商业道德了，整个事件也必然为怀疑提供理由。

在10月14日至10月25日期间，仅一家英国公司的发货量就被扣押并未经授权移至上述日本控制的工厂，这批货物包括2,337篮鸡蛋，价值约国币15万元。这些货物的提单仍由英国收货人持有。

当《字林西报》记者就该文章询问三井物产株式会社的一名官员时，该官员表示其公司无可奉告。他说，此事已由公司律师处理。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
NOV 15 1940
No. S.
268.3
SIRY
Extraordinary, Impossible Doctrine
AN EXTRAORDINARY LIGHT is cast upon
Japanese notions of developing China
through the Asia Development Board's admoni-
tion to one of the leading foreign egg com-
panies in Shanghai:
"All third Power packing companies must
stop buying eggs and stop interfering with Jap-
anese economic development in China."
This cordial invitation to business hara-kiri
will meet with a cold reception, beyond any
doubt. We cannot believe that the Japanese
would welcome any orders to quit doing busi-
ness in, say, the United States, even though
Americans themselves gave such orders (to
say nothing of their reaction if such an order
came from some complete outsider such as the
Mexicans or the Canadians.) Americans and
Britons correspondingly cannot join in glee at
such a move to shut them off from the China
field.
What the Asia Development Board de-
mands in an impossibility, unless foreigners are
to accept the principle that they must
clear out of China and stay out.
Eggs may come temporarily. We
hope it is not temporarily or otherwise, but
there is no use ignoring any possibility in such
extraordinary times. But as a fundamental
proposition it will never stand up indefinitely
and we regard it as extremely poor policy for
any Japanese (or other) organization to enun-
ciate such a bombastic and impossible notion.
It is bad enough for such a company as
the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha to misappropriate
valuable property. That has already taken toll
to the tune of ... a million dollars' worth of
eggs belonging to, and paid for by, the seven
foreign firms in the egg business here. Even
worse, however, from the standpoint of general
policy is this effort to drive the companies out
of the field altogether in the interest of "Jap-
anese economic development."
No responsible Japanese spokesman with
whom we have come in contact was willing to
stand sponsor for the theory that China must
become a complete Japanese monopoly—though
the facts have at times pretty well spoken for
themselves. We doubt if anyone is going out
on the limb so far as to assert that as a gen-
eral proposition, if for no other reason than
that the leaders know they need foreign as-
sistance and co-operation sooner or later. Yet
to enunciate such a doctrine for any single line
of business, such as the egg trade, is to invite
inquiry as to whether at least some lawless and
irresponsible Japanese elements do not wish to
extend the doctrine to cover all foreign busi-
ness in China.
It's too big a chew to bite off. Japan can-
not afford to isolate herself, which is precisely
what she is asking for if she asks for one-way
benefits—that is, for the privilege of dealing
with foreigners only in ways beneficial to her-
self alone. A more realistic viewpoint should
prevail with reference to all Japan's foreign
contacts. And the contact of her egg mono-
polists with the foreign egg traders will be an
excellent place to begin. In the long run,
crime doesn't pay.

1940年11月15日

268.3
SIRY

非凡且不可能的论调

亚洲开发委员会对上海一家主要外国鸡蛋公司发出的警告，为日本人的对华发展观念投下了一道非凡的光芒：
“所有第三国包装公司必须停止购买鸡蛋，停止干涉日本在中国的经济发展。”
这种邀请商界“切腹自尽”的友好提议，毫无疑问将受到冷遇。我们无法相信日本人会欢迎任何让他们退出在美国做生意的命令，即使是美国人自己发出这样的命令（更不用说如果这样的命令来自墨西哥人或加拿大人等完全的外来者，他们会作何反应）。同样，美国人和英国人也不能对这种将他们排除在中国市场之外的举动感到高兴。

除非外国人接受必须撤出中国并永远不得返回的原则，否则亚洲开发委员会的要求是不可能的。鸡蛋可能会暂时到来。我们希望这不是暂时的或其他情况，但在如此非凡的时期，忽视任何可能性都是无益的。但作为一个基本命题，它永远无法长期成立，我们认为任何日本（或其他）组织宣扬这种夸夸其谈且不可能的念头是极糟糕的政策。

像三井物产株式会社这样的公司侵吞贵重财产已经够糟糕了。这已经造成了代价……价值数百万美元的鸡蛋被侵吞，这些鸡蛋属于在此地从事鸡蛋业务的七家外国公司，并由它们付款。然而，从总体政策的角度来看，更糟糕的是为了“日本经济发展”的利益，试图将这些公司完全赶出该领域。

我们接触过的负责任的日本发言人中，没有人愿意为“中国必须成为日本的完全垄断区”这一理论背书——尽管事实有时已经很好地说明了这一点。我们怀疑是否有人会如此冒险地断言这是一个普遍命题，如果没有其他原因，至少是因为领导层知道他们迟早需要外国的援助与合作。然而，针对鸡蛋贸易等单一行业宣扬这样的论调，不禁让人质疑，是否至少有一些无法无天且不负责任的日本分子希望将这一论调扩展到涵盖所有在华外国业务。

这口气太大了，日本咬不动。日本承受不起自我孤立，而这正是她所要求的，如果她只要求单向利益的话——也就是说，只要求以仅对她自己有利的方式与外国人打交道的特权。在处理日本的所有对外接触时，应采取更现实的观点。而其鸡蛋垄断者与外国鸡蛋贸易商的接触将是一个极好的起点。从长远来看，犯罪是没有好结果的。

CHINA PRESS.

NOV 1 1 1938

Egg Controversy
The great egg controversy, finally, it would seem, is moving towards a settlement.
At any rate, the Japanese embassy spokesman, at the press conference last night, told foreign newspapermen that an amicable settlement of the egg controversy was confidently expected.
These happy expectations, he explained, were based on the results already obtained from a number of discussions by various interested parties.
Promptly, one local newshawk asked for details. "These haven't hatched yet," was the prompt reply.
But then, there is the story, recounted by a German citizen who resided in the United States during the World War. That before the United States entered the conflict, on several occasions he bought drafts at American banks and attempted to forward sums of money to Germany to meet life insurance premiums. On each occasion, he said, the letters were seized in England and the cancelled drafts returned to the banks. But, to add insult to injury, this German added, the drafts were cashed by the British Government and the money confiscated.
Perhaps, after all, it is not "dangerous thoughts" but cash that the censor is after.

看来，这场巨大的鸡蛋争议终于正走向解决。

随即，一名本地记者追问细节。“那些还没孵出来呢，”这是迅速的答复。
但是，还有一位在世界大战期间居住在美国的德国公民讲述的故事。他说，在美国参战之前，他曾几次在美国银行购买汇票，并试图汇款到德国以支付人寿保险费。他说，每次信件都在英国被扣押，作废的汇票被退回银行。但是，这位德国人补充说，为了侮辱人，英国政府兑现了这些汇票并没收了这笔钱。
也许，审查人员追求的毕竟不是“危险思想”，而是现金。

S. Kato To Hear

Nippon Envoy Arrives
For Third Power
Conversations

Coming to Shanghai to hold
talks with third power representa-
tives in this city, Mr. Sotomatsu
Kato, Japanese Minister-At-Large,
arrived last night from Tokyo.

He announced that his talks
might be considered as parallel
to those which the Foreign Mini-
ster, Admiral K. Nomura, is hav-
ing with the American and Bri-
tish Ambassadors to Tokyo Mr.
Joseph Grew and Sir Robert
Craigie.

Egg Problem

Although no announcement has
been made to this effect, it is
considered possible that Mr. Kato
might be asked to look into the
egg problem, in which the Mitsui
Bussan Kaisha interests have
been appropriating cargoes for
which American and British firms
have already paid hard cash in
the Yangtzê delta, and already
suffered losses estimated at $500,-
000.

While official representations to
Tokyo will no doubt continue to
be made through the officially ac-
credited ambassadors, collateral
talks might prove of value, for
eign business men consider. For

might look into the latest at-
tempt to slam the open door good
and tight, a form letter which
must be signed by foreign firms
before they may be allowed to buy

Form Letter

The form letter reads: "To the
Shanghai branch of the Mitsui
Bussan Kaisha—We hereby pledge
that the....baskets of hen eggs
we ship to Shanghai today will be
delivered to your company on ar-
rival without fail, and we agree

market, in direct defiance of the
Open Door principle which the
Japanese say they are following,

present efforts being made in
Japan to improve relations with
America and Britain.

《上海晚邮报及信使报》。

1939年11月9日

加藤将听取
关于鸡蛋盗窃案的汇报

日本特使抵沪
进行第三方
会谈

日本特命全权公使加藤素松（Sotomatsu Kato）先生昨晚从东京抵达，前来上海与驻沪第三方代表举行会谈。

他宣布，他的会谈可被视为与外相野村吉三郎海军上将（Admiral K. Nomura）在东京同美国大使约瑟夫·格鲁（Joseph Grew）先生和英国大使罗伯特·克雷吉爵士（Sir Robert Craigie）进行的会谈平行。

鸡蛋问题

虽然尚未就此发布公告，但人们认为加藤先生可能会被要求调查鸡蛋问题，在该问题中，三井物产株式会社的利益方一直在侵占英美公司已在长江三角洲支付现金购买的货物，造成的损失估计已达 500,000 美元。

虽然通过正式认证的大使向东京提出的官方交涉无疑将继续进行，但外商认为，附带性的会谈可能证明具有价值。例如，他们说，加藤先生可能会调查最近企图彻底关闭“门户开放”政策的最新举动，即一份必须由各外国公司签署的格式信函，只有签署后他们才被允许在三角洲地区购买鸡蛋。

格式信函

该格式信函写道：“致三井物产株式会社上海分社——兹保证，我方今日运往上海的……篮鲜鸡蛋将在抵达时毫无例外地交付给贵公司，并同意按照日本鸡蛋协会……鸡蛋公司……确定的价格付款。（签名）代表。昭和14年……月……日。”

外国公司指出，通过签署这封信，他们只是将鸡蛋白白送给 MBK。如果不凭此信就不允许他们贸易，他们就被完全拒之市场门外，这直接违背了日本人声称遵循的“门户开放”原则，也与日本目前为改善与美国和英国关系所做的努力直接矛盾。

"COUNCIL MEMBER, KING OF PIRATES"

We have now obtained the following information
about the recent serious hold-up in the egg supply:-

警方和领事当局昨日正在调查有关便衣日本人在北部和东部地区“没收”属于外国公司的鸡蛋货物的指控。

据可靠消息来源，其中一起事件发生在一周前的百老汇路（Broadway）。据报道，身穿西式服装的日本人拦截了一辆卡车，该车正将112篮鸡蛋从北站运往杨树浦的一家英资包装公司。据说日本人占有了整批鸡蛋货物。

此前，许多 destined for 由英美公司包装的鸡蛋货物是通过黄浦江运入上海的。

日本驻上海首席海军武官野村N.海军少将（Vice-Admiral N. Nomura）在昨日的日本记者招待会上表示，如果关于虹口港以北发生扣押事件的报道属实，“肯定会采取适当措施”。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
OCT 28 1939
26238

Interference With Eggs Is
Basis Of Many Protests.

Consignments Of British And American Firms Have
Been Detained While Passing Through Settlement
Areas; Matter Is Now Under Negotiation

The repeated seizures of consignments of eggs owned by various British and American egg companies have been the subject of protests lodged by the British Consul-General, Sir Herbert Phillips, with the Japanese Consul-General, Mr. Miura, and also the subject of inquiries at the American Consulate-General.

An official at the British Consulate yesterday told "The Shanghai Times" that the Consul-General had protested to the Japanese authorities over the seizure of a truckload of 112 baskets of eggs, belonging to a British egg concern, in Hongkew, on October 21. The truck, loaded with eggs, had been proceeding from the company's godown in Hongkew, when it was halted and the 112 baskets of eggs seized by Japanese, "presumably employees of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha," a shipping company interested in the export of eggs.

The protest was lodged soon after the seizure, but "no specific reply has as yet been received," the official stated. "However, the matter is under negotiation." The British egg company concerned demanded the return of the eggs from the M.B.K., and finally, last Thursday, they were returned to the rightful owners.

However, another truck loaded with eggs was seized by these same Japanese yesterday morning, it was stated. This seizure also took place in Hongkew in the International Settlement. The British Consul-General is again protesting to the Japanese Consul-General, and the official at the Consulate stated that he would continue to do so as long as British property was seized. Each protest also asked that the Japanese authorities take steps to prevent a repetition of such incidents.

Another Yesterday
The second case of seizure of eggs occurred yesterday morning, but the British egg company concerned took the precaution in loading only 30 baskets of eggs on the truck, in case of seizure.

The official at the British Consulate also stated that the egg concerns, whose trucks have been subjected to these incident, had written numerous letters of protest to the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and had also called at the latter's offices to bring these actions to an end. On one such visit, the officials of the M.B.K. had asked the British company's representatives to sign a letter, exonerating the M.B.K. from all blame. The British company had refused. "The Japanese" then asked them to agree not to buy eggs in Nanking, but again the visitors refused.

Finally, the M.B.K. agreed to the unconditional return of the truckload of eggs to the British owners. Other British and American companies have also protested to the M.B.K., besides reporting the matter to their respective Consulates and Embassies, it was stated.

Admiral Nomura Questioned
At the press conference yesterday, Vice-Admiral Nomura, the chief Japanese naval officer in Shanghai, who was present with a number of other naval officers, told correspondents that he had just returned from Nanking, where he had discussed the egg problem with the authorities there. Questions of this kind were bound to arise here in Shanghai, and that he was doing everything in his power to prevent unfortunate incidents.

Asked if he were aware of the seizure of a truckload of eggs yesterday morning, the Admiral replied that "if reports of this seizure are correct, steps will be taken to rectify the situation; however, we have no knowledge of such action."

《字林西报》。
1939年10月28日
26238

干扰鸡蛋运输是
许多抗议的起因。

英美商行的货物在通过租界区域时被扣留；此事目前正在谈判中

多家英美蛋业公司拥有的鸡蛋货物屡遭扣押，英国总领事赫伯特·菲利普斯爵士（Sir Herbert Phillips）已就此向日本总领事三浦先生提出抗议，美国总领事馆也就此进行了查询。

英国领事馆一名官员昨日告诉《字林西报》，总领事已就10月21日在虹口扣押一辆载有112篮鸡蛋的卡车一事向日本当局提出抗议，该批鸡蛋属于一家英国蛋业公司。这辆满载鸡蛋的卡车正从该公司位于虹口的仓库出发，途中被日本人拦下，112篮鸡蛋被扣押，据信扣押者是“三井物产株式会社”的员工，这是一家从事鸡蛋出口业务的航运公司。

抗议在扣押发生后不久即提出，但该官员称，“目前尚未收到具体答复”。“不过，此事正在谈判中。”相关的英国蛋业公司向三井物产株式会社要求归还鸡蛋，最终在上周四，鸡蛋被归还给合法所有者。

然而，据称昨天上午，另一辆满载鸡蛋的卡车又被同样的日本人扣押。这次扣押也发生在公共租界的虹口地区。英国总领事再次向日本总领事提出抗议，领事馆官员表示，只要英国财产遭到扣押，他将继续提出抗议。每次抗议还要求日本当局采取措施，防止此类事件重演。

昨日另有一案
第二起鸡蛋扣押案发生在昨天上午，但相关的英国蛋业公司采取了预防措施，仅在卡车上装载了30篮鸡蛋，以防被扣押。

英国领事馆官员还表示，卡车遭受此类事件的蛋业公司已向三井物产株式会社发出多封抗议信，并前往其办公室交涉，以制止这些行为。在一次这样的访问中，三井物产株式会社的官员要求英国公司代表签署一封信，免除三井物产株式会社的所有责任。英国公司予以拒绝。随后，“日本人”要求他们同意不在南京购买鸡蛋，但来访者再次拒绝。

最终，三井物产株式会社同意无条件将整车鸡蛋归还给英国所有者。据称，其他英美公司除了向各自的领事馆和大使馆报告此事外，也已向三井物产株式会社提出抗议。

询问野村中将
在昨天的记者招待会上，上海日本海军最高指挥官野村中将与其他几名海军军官一同出席，他对记者表示，他刚从南京回来，在那里他与当地当局讨论了鸡蛋问题。这类问题在上海必然会出现，他正在尽其所能防止不幸事件的发生。

当被问及是否知晓昨天上午扣押一车鸡蛋的事件时，野村中将回答说，“如果有关此次扣押的报道属实，将采取措施纠正局势；然而，我们对此类行动并不知情。”

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 28 1939
Shipments Said
“Hijacked” By
Japanese Firm
British, America Houses
Deprived Of Over
500,000 Eggs
TRUCKLOAD TAKEN
IN SETTLEMENT
Industry Formerly Third
Largest Of Exports
From China

Foreign egg packers in Shanghai
are being “starved out” of supplies
by an internationally-known
Japanese firm, which has resorted
to “hijacking” measures to complete its plan of effecting a monopoly over the industry, it was
charged here yesterday.
Informed quarters which released
this information to the press yesterday indicated that since October
10, no less than 500,000 eggs had
been “stolen” by the Japanese firm
ostensibly acting under instructions
from the Japanese military headquarters.
According to the information received, seven of the largest packers
in Shanghai, including two American and five British, are being
deprived of their merchandise. The
seizures, it was added, had been
fully reported to the consular authorities concerned.
Eggs Sent To England
The firm referred to, according
to the information received, was
the Mitsui Busan Kaisha which,
after “appropriating” the eggs,
packed and sold them to buyers in
Great Britain.
Interviewed by a foreign correspondent, the manager of the Mitsui
firm here was said to have said
“the eggs were taken for the Navy,
and it was, therefore, up to the
Navy to find them.”
While these were not the first
losses sustained by local egg
packers, trading circles indicated
that for the first time, they faced
a complete shut-out of supplies
from the Koripo areas.
A packer told THE CHINA PRESS
that ever since the outbreak of the
Sino-Japanese hostilities in these
areas, the egg trade had faced considerable obstacles set up by the
Japanese.
Buy Through Japanese
For a time, however, he added,
packers were still able to obtain
eggs regardless how stringent the
regulations were which governed
dealers purchasing in the producing areas. He stated that all packers bought through small Japanese
agents who also obtained for the
foreigners the necessary passes for
their purchases.
Since October 10, he added, even
this arrangement has not satisfied
the Japanese. “They allowed the
eggs to get into Japanese ships
coming down the Yangtse River;
they even tried to collect the
freight charges, but they disallowed
the delivery of the eggs to the
consignees.”
Asked whether the eggs might
have been mistaken for Chinese
property, the packer interviewed
stated that to his knowledge every
case was clearly marked with the
name of the foreign consignee and
his address.

page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》。
1939年10月28日
称货物被
日本公司
“劫持”
英、美商行
损失超过
50万枚鸡蛋
卡车货物在
租界内被夺
该行业曾是中国
第三大出口产业

据昨日在此间指控，上海的外国鸡蛋包装商正被一家国际知名的日本公司“断绝”供应，该公司采取“劫持”手段，以实现其垄断该行业的计划。

昨日向媒体发布此消息的消息灵通人士指出，自10月10日以来，至少有50万枚鸡蛋被这家日本公司“窃取”，该公司表面上是奉日本军事总部之令行事。

根据收到的信息，上海七家最大的包装商，包括两家美商和五家英商，正被剥夺其货物。此外，这些扣押事件已向有关领事当局作了全面报告。

鸡蛋运往英国
根据收到的信息，所指的这家公司是三井物产株式会社，该公司在“没收”鸡蛋后，将其包装并出售给英国的买家。

一位外国记者采访了该三井公司在上海的经理，据说他表示“鸡蛋是被海军拿走的，因此应由海军去寻找它们。”

虽然这并非本地鸡蛋包装商遭受的首次损失，但贸易界人士表示，这是他们第一次面临来自高邮地区的供应完全中断的局面。

一位包装商告诉《大美晚报》，自从这些地区的中日敌对行动爆发以来，鸡蛋贸易就面临着日本人设置的巨大障碍。

通过日本人购买

然而，他补充说，在一段时间内，尽管在产区采购受到严格规定的限制，包装商仍能够获得鸡蛋。他表示，所有包装商都通过小型日本代理商进行购买，这些代理商还为外国人办理采购所需的通行证。

他补充说，自10月10日以来，甚至连这种安排也无法满足日本人的要求。“他们允许鸡蛋装上沿长江而下的日本船只；他们甚至试图收取运费，但他们不允许将鸡蛋交付给收货人。”

当被问及鸡蛋是否可能被误认为是中国财产时，接受采访的包装商表示，据他所知，每箱货物都清楚地标明了外国收货人的姓名和地址。
26253

page_data.en:
26254

Nippon Ships Used
Because Japanese shipping firms
now practically hold a monopoly
over the Yangtse trade, the in-
formant continued, the packers are
forced to put their cargo on
Japanese vessels. This, he added,
greatly facilitated the "plundering"
of the large Japanese house.
A seizure which was made right
here in Shanghai was revealed by
the packer. The victim was a
British firm which was transport-
ing on October 24 some 112 baskets
of eggs. While passing through
Broadway, the truck was hijacked
by employees of the Mitsui Bussan
Kaisha and was ordered to deliver
the goods to the M.B.K. godown.
Commenting on the report of the
seizure last night, Admiral Nomura
told correspondents at the press
conference that he had no infor-
mation of the incident. He pro-
mised that if the report were true,
steps would be taken to rectify such
conditions.
Solution Sought
The Admiral also explained that
"there are bound to be questions
arising in this large area of the
nature of the egg situation." He
said while in Nanking recently he
made efforts to obtain a satisfactory
solution to the problems.
Regarding the lifting of restric-
tions to facilitate business here, the
Admiral went on, "it must be
pointed out that the hostilities are
still under way. But measures are
already being considered to relax
various restrictions.
"It is not solely a question of
the Navy or of the Army, but
there are various other agencies
involved as well as those authori-
ties on the spot which are directly
or indirectly concerned."
100,000 Tons A Year
The egg packing industry in
China formerly was the third
largest export industry of the entire
Chinese nation. Each year, from
40,000 to 50,000 tons of frozen eggs
and a like amount of shelled eggs
were exported to foreign countries.
Calculated at about $22 per 100
pounds of eggs, which was the rate
before the war, the egg business in
China reached the huge total of
approximately $50,000,000.
Since the war, however, the busi-
ness had dropped considerably. In-
creasing difficulties in purchasing
and in obtaining transportation
service to move the eggs to Shang-
hai were regarded as two of the
most important causes.
page_data.zh:
26254

使用日本船只

由于日本航运公司现在实际上垄断了长江贸易，消息人士继续说道，包装商被迫将货物装上日本船只。他补充说，这极大地方便了这家大型日本商行的“掠夺”。

一位包装商披露了一起就在上海发生的扣押事件。受害者是一家英国公司，该公司于10月24日运输约112篮鸡蛋。当卡车经过百老汇路（Broadway）时，被三井物产株式会社的员工劫持，并被命令将货物送至三井物产株式会社的仓库。

野村中将昨晚在评论有关扣押的报道时，在记者招待会上告诉记者，他没有关于此事件的信息。他承诺，如果报道属实，将采取措施纠正此类状况。

寻求解决方案

野村中将还解释说，“在这个广大地区，像鸡蛋这样的情况必然会引起一些问题。”他说，最近他在南京时，曾努力寻求令人满意的解决方案。

关于解除限制以促进此地商业的问题，野村中将接着说，“必须指出，敌对行动仍在进行中。但已经在考虑采取措施放宽各种限制。”

“这不仅仅是海军或陆军的问题，还有其他各种机构以及直接或间接有关的当地当局参与其中。”

每年10万吨

中国的鸡蛋包装业曾经是整个中国第三大出口产业。每年有4万至5万吨冰蛋和同等数量的去壳鸡蛋出口到国外。按战前每100磅鸡蛋约22美元的价格计算，中国的鸡蛋业务总额达到了约5,000万美元的巨大规模。

然而，自战争爆发以来，该业务大幅下降。采购困难以及将鸡蛋运往上海的运输服务难以获得，被视为两个最重要的原因。

26235
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

OCT 27 1939

U.S. And British
Firms Suffering
'In New Racket

MBK Employees Hijack
Truck Travelling
On Broadway

ROBBERIES TOTAL
5125 BASKETS

Consignments Shipped
From Delta Seized
By Nipponese

Two American and Five
British egg packing plants
in Shanghai are being de-
prived of eggs, bought by
them upcountry, by a
Japanese firm whose cul-
minating audacity has been
the seizure in Broadway of a
truckload containing 122 bas-
kets.
In the fortnight October 10-
24 no less than 5215 baskets,
each containing 800 eggs,
have been stolen and taken to
the Whangpoo Road plant of the
Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, who have
been breaking up the eggs and
selling them in bulk to Great
Britain.
Protests Prepared
These wholesale robberies have
been duly reported to the Amer-
ican and British embassies, and
are expected to form the basis of
yet another protest to the Tokyo
government. In the meantime the
firms are being starved, and very
few cargoes are getting through.
The Mitsui Bussan Kaisha egg
refrigerating and packing plant is
that of the China Egg Product
Company, who were practically
forced out of their premises in
Whangpoo Road. It is nominally
known as the Yangtze Egg Com-
pany, but is owned and operated
by the MBK.

（批：File C 26/10）
page_data.zh:
26235
《上海晚邮报与水星报》。

1939年10月27日

英美商行
在新勒索中
遭受损失

三井物产员工劫持
行驶在百老汇路上的
卡车

抢劫总数达
5125篮

从三角洲地区运出的
货物被日本人扣押

上海的两家美商和五家英商鸡蛋包装厂被一家日本公司剥夺了其在外地购买的鸡蛋，该公司胆大妄为的顶峰是在百老汇路扣押了一辆装有122篮鸡蛋的卡车。

在10月10日至24日的两周内，不少于5215篮鸡蛋（每篮装800枚）被盗，并被运至三井物产株式会社位于黄浦路（Whangpoo Road）的工厂，该公司将这些鸡蛋打碎，并批量出售给英国。

准备抗议

这些大规模抢劫事件已正式报告给美国和英国大使馆，预计将成为向东京政府提出另一次抗议的依据。与此同时，各公司正面临断供，很少有货物能够通过。

三井物产株式会社的鸡蛋冷藏和包装厂原属中国蛋品公司（China Egg Product Company），该公司实际上被迫迁出其在黄浦路的场所。该厂名义上称为扬子蛋业公司（Yangtze Egg Company），但由三井物产株式会社拥有和经营。

（批注：档案 C 26/10）

page_data.en:
Bought In Delta
Method of purchasing eggs is
for purchasing agents of the vari-
ous firms to visit producing areas
in the delta and pay cash for con-
signments. These are sent to
shipping ports, where Japanese
ships are about the only ones al-
lowed to take the cargoes. Freight
is calculated, at the shipping port,
but is only payable on arrival at
Shanghai. Some cargoes are
brought in by the Shanghai-Nan-
king Railway.
What has been happening as re-
gards ships is that delivery in
Shanghai has been refused. Firms
that go to take normal delivery of
an egg cargo was told that orders
had been given to deliver the
goods to the MBK, not the proper
consignee.
Freight Bill Demand
Despite the fact that the ship-
ping concern had delivered a
cargo, bought by and consigned to
a British firm, to the MBK, it has
had the audacity on a recent
occasion to send the freight bill
to the actual consignee, which
naturally refused to pay.
Ninety percent of the egg pro-
ducts exports from Shanghai be-
fore the European War were sent
to Great Britain, and this figure
is believed to be higher now. And
the MBK actually has been seiz-
ing eggs, the property of American
and British firms, and preparing
them for export to Great Britain
itself.
Seizure On Truck
The truckload seizure by em-
ployees of the MBK on Broadway
of egg belonging to the British Egg
Packing and Cold Storage Com-
pany (located in Yangtzepoo) fol-
lowed the arrival of a cargo at
Markham Road station, whence
the truck actually managed to
take delivery of 112 baskets.
This seizure actually inside the
International Settlement appears
to have worried the consciences of
the MBK officials, who later wrote
to the British firm concerned,
offering to return the eggs if the
firm would write a letter saying
that it "realized that the MBK
had made a mistake." The British
firm has refused to do this. So
the situation remains at present.
page_data.zh:
在三角洲地区购买

各家公司的采购代理前往三角洲地区的产地，以现金支付货款购买鸡蛋。这些货物被运往港口，在那里几乎只有日本船只被允许承运货物。运费在装运港计算，但仅在抵达上海时支付。部分货物由沪宁铁路运入。

关于船只方面发生的情况是，在上海拒绝交付货物。那些前去正常提取鸡蛋货物的公司被告知，已下达命令将货物交付给三井物产株式会社，而不是正确的收货人。

索要运费单

尽管航运公司将一批由一家英国公司购买并指定为其收货人的货物交付给了三井物产株式会社，但该公司在最近的一次事件中竟厚颜无耻地向实际收货人发送运费账单，后者自然拒绝支付。

在欧洲战争爆发前，上海出口的鸡蛋产品有百分之九十运往英国，据信这一比例现在更高。而三井物产株式会社实际上一直在扣押属于英美公司的鸡蛋，并将其准备出口到英国本身。

卡车上的扣押

三井物产株式会社员工在百老汇路扣押属于英国鸡蛋包装冷藏公司（位于杨树浦）的鸡蛋，此前有一批货物抵达马克姆路（Markham Road）车站，卡车实际上设法从那里提取了112篮鸡蛋。

这次实际上发生在公共租界内部的扣押似乎让三井物产株式会社的官员良心不安，他们后来写信给相关的英国公司，提出如果该公司写一封信表示“意识到三井物产株式会社犯了错误”，则愿意归还鸡蛋。该英国公司拒绝这样做。因此，目前的局势依然如此。
